# How to Use Shopify in the Philippines: Store Setup, Payments, and Apps


Shopify is one of the most popular ways Philippine businesses make that move. It's built for people who want to run a serious online store without needing a developer on speed dial. In this guide, we'll walk you through how to set it up – from creating your account to accepting payments from Filipino customers – so you can go live with confidence.


## **What Is Shopify and Why Are Philippine Businesses Using It?**


Shopify is an e-commerce platform that lets you build and manage an online store. You get a website, a product catalog, an order management system, and a checkout — all in one place. No need to stitch together different tools or hire someone to build you a website from scratch.


For Philippine businesses specifically, Shopify has become a go-to platform for a few reasons:


- **It's built for selling.** Unlike a regular website builder, everything in Shopify is designed around getting products in front of customers and converting them.
- **It handles the technical side.** Hosting, security, and updates are managed for you. You focus on the business.
- **It scales with you.** Whether you're fulfilling 100 or 10,000 orders a month, the platform handles it.
- **It connects to local payment methods.** With the right setup, you can accept GCash, Maya, credit and debit cards, and even bank transfers; the same methods your customers already use.


Shopify pricing starts at around $23/month on the Basic plan. It's not free, but for a business that's ready to grow online, it's a serious tool worth the investment.


## **How to Set Up Your Shopify Store in the Philippines**


### Step 1: Create Your Account


Go to[shopify.com](https://www.shopify.com/ph?ref=paymongo-blog.ghost.io) and start a free trial. You'll enter your email, create a password, and answer a few questions about your business. You don't need a credit card to start.


Once you're in, you'll land on the Shopify admin, your store's control center. This is where you'll manage everything: products, orders, customers, settings.


### Step 2: Choose and Customize Your Theme


Your theme is your store's look and feel. Shopify has a Theme Store with free and paid options. For most businesses just starting out, a free theme works well.


When choosing a theme, think about:


- **Mobile first.** Most of your Filipino customers will be on their phones. Pick a theme that looks clean on mobile.
- **Load speed.** Faster stores convert better. Avoid theme that are heavy on animations.
- **Your product type.** A fashion store needs different layouts than a food business or a service-based business.


Once you've picked a theme, customize it with your logo, brand colors, and fonts. You don't need to know any code, it's all drag and drop.


### Step 3: Add Your Products


Go to **Products > Add product** and start building your catalog. For each product, you'll want:


- A clear, descriptive product name
- A well-written description (focus on benefits, not just features)
- High-quality photos; multiple angles if possible
- Price in Philippine Peso (PHP)
- Inventory count if you're tracking stock
- Variants if you sell different sizes, colors, or options


Take the time to write good product descriptions. This is also where SEO lives – customers searching Google for what you sell can find you through your product pages.


### Step 4: Organize Your Collections


Collections are Shopify's version of categories — they group your products so customers can browse by type, use case, or occasion. Think of them as the sections of a physical store: a rack for tops, a shelf for accessories, a table for sale items.


You can create two types:


- Manual collections: you handpick which products belong in each group
- Automated collections: products are added automatically based on rules you set (e.g., any product tagged "new arrival" appears in the New Arrivals collection)


For most Philippine businesses, useful collections include product type (e.g., Bags, Clothing, Home), occasion (e.g., Christmas Gifts, Back to School), or promo status (e.g., Sale, Bestsellers). Well-organized collections also help your store rank on Google — each collection page can target its own keyword.


To create one, go to **Products > Collections > Create collection** .


### Step 5: Create Product Categories


Shopify uses a standardized product taxonomy to categorize your items. This is separate from collections and matters mostly for Google Shopping and Meta (Facebook/Instagram) ads.


Go to each product and assign it a category from Shopify's built-in taxonomy. For example: *Apparel & Accessories > Clothing > Tops & T-Shirts, or Food, Beverages & Tobacco > Food Items > Snacks* . This ensures your products are correctly classified when you connect sales channels and run ads.


### Step 6: Add Sales Channels


One of Shopify's biggest advantages is that it lets you sell across multiple platforms from a single admin. Your inventory, orders, and customer data stay in sync no matter where the sale happens.


From your Shopify admin, go to Sales Channels and consider adding:


- Facebook & Instagram Shop – essential for Philippine businesses; a large portion of local online shoppers discover products through these platforms
- TikTok Shop – fast-growing in the Philippines, especially for consumer goods
- Google – gets your products into Google Shopping results and Google Search ads
- Lazada or Shopee – available through third-party apps on the Shopify App Store


You don't need to activate all of them at once. Start with the channel where your customers already spend time, then expand.


### Step 7: Set Up Shipping


Go to **Settings > Shipping and Delivery** . Here you'll define your shipping zones and rates.


For Philippine businesses, common approaches include:


- Free shipping on orders above a certain amount (e.g., ₱2,000). This is effective for increasing average order value.
- Flat rate shipping; this is simple and predictable for customers.
- Calculated rates, when you charged based on weight and destination.


For couriers, J&T Express, LBC, and Ninja Van are popular integrations for Philippine Shopify stores. Some have Shopify apps that let you generate waybills and track shipments directly from your admin.


### Step 8: Configure Your Store Settings


Before going live, check these:


- Currency: Set to Philippine Peso (PHP) under **Settings > Store details**
- Taxes: Shopify can calculate taxes automatically, but review this with your accountant given BIR requirements.
- Checkout settings: Decide whether customers need to create an account or can check out as guests (guest checkout usually converts better).
- Contact info and policies: Add your return policy, privacy policy, and contact page. These build trust with Filipino buyers.


## **How to Accept Payments on Shopify in the Philippines**


Here's something important to know before you launch: **Shopify Payments – Shopify's built-in payment processor – is not available in the Philippines.**


That means you'll need to connect a[third-party payment gateway](https://www.paymongo.com/products/accept-payments/plugins?ref=paymongo-blog.ghost.io) or plug-in to accept online payments. This is standard for Philippine Shopify stores, so don't let it slow you down. It just means adding one more step to your setup.


Use PayMongo as your Shopify payment gateway.


[Sign Up](https://dashboard.paymongo.com/signup?ref=paymongo-blog.ghost.io)


When you use a third-party gateway, Shopify charges an additional transaction fee (depending on your plan, on top of whatever your gateway charges). This is worth factoring into your pricing.


Your payment gateway is the engine behind your checkout; it's what processes card payments, GCash, Maya, and bank transfers. For Philippine businesses, you want a gateway that:


- Accepts GCash and Maya (not optional – these are how a huge portion of Filipino customers prefer to pay)
- Supports credit and debit cards (Visa, Mastercard)
- Is licensed by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP)
- Has fast, reliable payouts in PHP


## **Setting Up a PayMongo Plugin on Shopify**


[PayMongo](https://www.paymongo.com/?ref=paymongo-blog.ghost.io) is a BSP-licensed financial operating system built specifically for Philippine businesses. It accepts e-wallets, QR Ph, credit and debit cards, and direct bank debit. It integrates directly with Shopify as an official app.


Here's how to connect it to your store:


**Step 1: Create a PayMongo account**


Go to[dashboard.paymongo.com](https://dashboard.paymongo.com/?ref=paymongo-blog.ghost.io) and sign up. You'll go through a quick verification process to activate your account.


**Step 2: Find PayMongo in the Shopify App Store**


From your Shopify admin, go to **Apps > Visit Shopify App Store** and search for "PayMongo." Install the official PayMongo app.


**Step 3: Connect your PayMongo account**


Once installed, the app will ask for your PayMongo API keys. Get these from your PayMongo dashboard under **Developers > API Keys** . Copy and paste your live public and secret keys into the Shopify app.


**Step 4: Set PayMongo as your payment provider**


Go to Settings > Payments in your Shopify admin. Under "Third-party providers," select PayMongo. Enable the payment methods you want to offer — GCash, Maya, cards, and more.


**Step 5: Test your checkout**


Before going live, run a test transaction to make sure everything is working. PayMongo provides test credentials so you can simulate a payment without real money moving.


Once this is set up, your customers will see GCash, Maya, and card options at checkout, exactly what they expect from a trustworthy Philippine online store.

Connects your store to multiple Philippine couriers, so you can compare rates, print waybills, and track shipments from one place.

Live chat and customer support tools. Important for Philippine buyers who often want to ask questions before committing to a purchase.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


#### Can I use Shopify in the Philippines?


Yes. Shopify is fully available in the Philippines. You can set up a store, sell to local and international customers, and manage everything from your Shopify admin. The main thing to note is that Shopify Payments is not available here, so you'll need to connect a third-party payment gateway like PayMongo.


#### What payment methods can I accept on Shopify in the Philippines?


With a gateway like PayMongo or Maya, you can accept GCash, Maya, Visa, Mastercard, and bank transfers. These cover the most popular payment methods among Filipino online shoppers.


#### How much does Shopify cost in the Philippines?


Shopify's Basic plan starts at around $23/month (roughly ₱1,400/month). There's also a 3-day free trial to get started. Keep in mind that transaction fees apply when using a third-party payment gateway.


#### Do I need a business registration to use Shopify in the Philippines?


You don't need to be registered to open a Shopify store. However, to fully activate a PayMongo account and accept payments, you'll need to complete identity and business verification. DTI registration (for sole proprietors) or SEC registration (for corporations/partnerships) is typically required.


#### Is PayMongo safe to use?


Yes. PayMongo is licensed by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) and is PCI-DSS compliant, which means it meets international standards for secure payment processing.
